_comment: The two real milestone buildings the user drew/commissioned and added on
2026-08-15: BIT Mesra and KFUPM. These are the places the Experience map is
actually about, so unlike every other pack here they are not stand-ins.
SAME PROBLEM AS THE DESERT PACK, DIFFERENT CAUSE. They look like pixel art
and are not: BIT Mesra is 2400x1792 with 79,965 distinct colours, KFUPM is
3776x1120 with 46,547, and a 1:1 crop shows smooth gradients across a wall
with no pixel grid anywhere. Colour-run length is 1.26 and 1.28 against a
valley band of 2.0-4.1. They go through tools/desert-pixelate.py for exactly
the reasons its docstring gives.
ONE DIFFERENCE: THERE IS NO DROP SHADOW. The semi-transparent alpha band on
these two has a mean luma of 74 and 85 — that is edge anti-aliasing, not a
shadow (the desert pack's band measured 2-16, i.e. black). SHADOW_CUT still
does the right thing here: it hardens the anti-aliased edge and trims to the
content box, which is what pixel art wants.
SIZES. Both are landmark-scale, pitched against instAcademic (245x107), the
largest thing already on the map. Widths are set from how much of the 44-tile
map each should command and heights follow the source aspect ratio, so
neither is squashed:
BIT Mesra  2280x1314 content, aspect 1.74 -> 256x148  (16 x 9.3 tiles)
KFUPM      3776x1120 content, aspect 3.37 -> 320x95   (20 x 5.9 tiles)
KFUPM is deliberately the widest thing on the map. The real campus reads as a
long low arcade and shrinking it to house scale would lose the one silhouette
that identifies it.
NO flatten. These are architectural: window mullions, arcade columns and
stair treads are one or two pixels wide at these sizes and a median filter
eats them. 20 colours holds the masonry without smearing the detail.
LICENCE: the user's own assets. Nothing to resolve, unlike the packs in
HANDOFF §9.10.
Regenerate: python tools/desert-pixelate.py --manifest=tools/campus-pack.json --sheet --compare
